bug_semantics: POST /company/save accepted a company logo without server-side type, extension, size, or SVG-content validation. An authenticated user satisfying the route's create company and update company permission gates could upload an SVG containing an embedded script; the controller derived a .svg destination name and wrote it to public storage. The resulting /storage/company/{slug}/{file} resource was served statically outside Laravel authentication, so direct navigation by any visitor executed attacker-controlled JavaScript in the application origin.
flaw_origin: dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c is the smallest true BIC: it first added the logo multipart field (explicitly accepting image/svg), copied an uploaded logo under the public webroot using the content-derived extension, and performed no validation. Later controller extraction, formatting, repository refactoring, and the 2026 public-disk rewrite preserved the same unrestricted-upload decision rather than introducing it.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` shows human author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, the sole message `Company custom logo.`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: The Secur0 CNA record https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-78337-unrestricted-upload-company-logo-svg-xss identifies CompanySaveController::save at POST /company/save, the authenticated create-company plus update-company permission prerequisite, direct-navigation stored SVG XSS, affected versions before 5.15.13, BIC dbd8f149, and patch aaa4fc76. It also states that every existing tag is vulnerable and that the fix is not tagged.

In the validated clone, `git show --format=fuller --patch dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` shows the BIC adding `request->file('logo')->extension()`, copying the upload to `public/asset/upload/company/{slug}/{timestamp}.{extension}`, saving the filename, and adding a multipart file input whose accept list includes image/svg. `git log --all -S"request->file('logo')" -- app/Http/Controllers` returns dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c as the first writer.

Direct parent verification is reproducible with `git show 4f6c90f21a3b1c826f65d554572c87647994e055:app/Http/Controllers/CompanyController.php`: save() only copies scalar company fields and has no logo field, file access, extension derivation, public write, or equivalent upload path. `git cat-file -p dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` confirms that exact commit's sole parent is 4f6c90f21a3b1c826f65d554572c87647994e055.

Lifecycle checks: `git show --find-renames 3f8ead9e0aafe1293253eab52eb72adb80be5b87` shows the existing vulnerable method renamed/extracted from CompanyController to Company/CompanySaveController; `git log -L 41,52:app/Http/Controllers/Company/CompanySaveController.php 54713abef6a89fdd3d9534c06f232dcecae4f6ca` traces the upload through the formatting-only caef09bb28dd80b8e19802b2c4a07ee619df0e84 change back to dbd8f149 and shows 4c15d20a57c4225bb3853bad2c5b01b3da11121f merely replacing the public-webroot copy with `storeAs(..., 'public')` while retaining the unvalidated extension. Thus neither the move nor later rewrite is the BIC.

At vulnerable parent 54713abef6a89fdd3d9534c06f232dcecae4f6ca, `routes/module/company.php` chains `can('create company')` and `can('update company')` on POST /company/save; CompanySaveController also checks create versus update authorization and company ownership. Its upload block calls `storeAs($folder, $filename, 'public')` with no validation. `config/filesystems.php` maps the public disk to storage/app/public, URL APP_URL/storage, and public/storage symlink; the logo views use /storage/company/{slug}/{logo}.

`git show --format=fuller --patch aaa4fc76bf039d5011884b86b8f29ddd50d17b17` shows the direct one-parent fix replacing the raw Request with CompanySaveRequest, validating logo MIME/size, and applying ValidateSafeSvg, which rejects script tags, event handlers, javascript: URLs, iframe, object, and embed content before storage. The same diff changes version.php from 5.15.12 in parent 54713abef6a89fdd3d9534c06f232dcecae4f6ca to 5.15.13. `git tag --contains dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` lists v1.0.0, v2.0.1, v4.6.0, v5.5.3, and v5.14.0; `git tag --contains aaa4fc76bf039d5011884b86b8f29ddd50d17b17` is empty, confirming all published tags are vulnerable and the 5.15.13 fix is untagged.
reasoning: The security invariant was missing from the feature's first implementation: untrusted file contents were accepted and made same-origin public content without a server-side allow-list or SVG neutralization. The immediate parent had no logo upload at all, while the BIC simultaneously created the input, persistence, and public serving path, so it is causally minimal. Subsequent refactors changed locations and storage APIs but preserved the dangerous acceptance semantics; permission work only narrowed who could upload. The direct fix closes the named SVG-script path by validating the request before storage and establishes the 5.15.12-to-5.15.13 boundary. AI attribution is judged exclusively from the BIC commit object, which has only a human identity and no AI marker; AI signals on later refactors or the fix are irrelevant under the protocol. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
